what: MR's accuracy read from the numbers the answers state, with no judge in the loop — and therefore the first reading in this repository whose error is not the judge's.
why: §13.185 screened every accepted answer for a name the gold does not state and reached 2 of MR's 84, because the golds are `2`, `$50`, `20%`, `3 days`, `$5,850`, `140 hours`. Multi-session reasoning on this dataset is arithmetic across sessions, so the channel that matters is the number. The arm ends its replies with its answer (`$60 / 5 = $12 per mug. 12`), so the last number is what it committed to, and comparing that with the gold's number needs no model.

artifact.why: the artifact the campaign is currently read from, and the one §13.184 audited the judge on

workflow: numeric-recheck.yml dispatched with run_id=41159983913, capability=MR (GitHub run 41177874270). The reading below was recomputed locally on the same downloaded artifact after the silent-denominator fix, which is why it counts 121 MR rows and the workflow's own output counted 113.

predictions.name: the judge's leniency reaches MR
predictions.registered: §13.184.5: MR's 87.25 is judge-limited, 19.38% x 121 = 23.5 questions of headroom
predictions.measured: 0 false accepts in the 80 readable accepted MR answers; Wilson 95% upper 4.6%

predictions.name: the two instruments agree on MR
predictions.measured: on the same 101 rows the numbers say 81 correct and the judge says 80. They disagree once, and the judge is the one that is wrong (92a0aa75, gold `1,5`, answer stated 1)

predictions.name: the audit's rate is a channel property, not an answer property
predictions.measured: the same screen on all five capabilities finds 2 false accepts in 209 readable accepted answers (1.0%, upper 3.4%), and both are outside MR. A judge that misses a swapped name at 44.90% is not a judge that accepts wrong numbers
predictions.verdict: consistent with the audit, and it constrains what the audit means

whatItChanges: MR's headline is no longer annotated 'judge-limited'. The annotation cost 23.5 hypothetical questions of headroom; the measurement finds 1 actual disagreement.
The head-to-head against the reference arm (87.25 against 103.75 on MR) is a memory finding, not a grading finding, on the numeric channel. The 16-question gap stands as published.

The audit's 19.38% keeps its own meaning — the judge does not verify names — but it can no longer be multiplied by 121 and quoted as MR error. It applies to the 119 accepted answers whose golds name anything, 2 of which are MR.
defectsFound: Silent denominator: the first `sourcesFrom` dropped rows whose `answer` was absent, which is every decline. MR lost 8 of 121 rows and nothing said so, because a decline is never correct and the numerator did not move. §13.186 records the reconciliation; the tool now prints `N of M unusable, no verdict` and keeps declines as `answer-unreachable`.
limits: Units are ignored. `3 days` against `72 hours` is called a difference; the class is small on MR but it is not zero.
Percentages are read as their number, so `20%` against `0.2` differs. A normaliser that guessed the scale would be deciding the answer.
Golds with no digits (`an hour and a half`) are unreachable: 4 of the 84 accepted MR answers, and 20 of 121 rows in total. They are excluded from the rate and counted beside it.

The stated-answer semantics hold where the answer is a value. On TR the same rule reads 28.3% judge-free accuracy, which is not a claim about TR — the answers there end with reasoning, not with a value. Only MR is read as an accuracy here.

It cannot see a wrong answer that keeps the gold's number. A reader that answers `3 people` to a gold of `3 days` agrees on this instrument and was accepted by the judge, so this bounds the number channel and not the capability.
